subject: Deployment mode & migration follow-up — Quanta Systems
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@quanta.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: deployment modes & migration path (quick recap + next steps)

Hi Daniel —

Great to meet you and the Quanta Systems team today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned on next steps:

What we heard
- Primary goal: move your internal question-answering/agent workflows off the legacy GPU cluster and reduce per-token cost while keeping sub-300ms tail latency for critical search flows.
- Current stack: mixed — some models via third-party LLM API (prod traffic), other workloads on a self-hosted cluster used for research and burst jobs.
- Key constraints: SOC2 compliance for PII, VPC networking for data ingress, predictable throughput for nightly batch jobs, and procurement wanting clear pricing for Dedicated or Private options.

Deployment modes we discussed (high level)
- Hosted API: fastest to start, minimal ops, good for low-to-medium throughput but limited to our hosted SLAs and shared tenancy.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (monthly commit), predictable throughput and isolation — good fit if you want consistent latency and cost predictability without managing infra.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full customer-managed network + optional on-prem package — required for data residency and strict compliance.

Migration considerations you flagged
- Seamless routing from current third-party API to Redwood hosted initially for eval traffic.
- Phase 2: migrate steady-state production to Dedicated for predictable spend and then evaluate Private for regulated datasets.
- KV/prefix cache reuse and prompt set alignment are important to avoid quality regressions during migration.

Suggested next steps
1) I’ll send a short mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones for a POC (2–4 weeks) and estimated pricing options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
2) Can we set a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week (Vivek + your infra lead) to walk through network/topology and SOC2 artefacts?
3) Please share the procurement contact and any baseline SLA/commit constraints.

Attachments: initial MAP draft + Dedicated pricing workbook (draft) — see links/attachments.

If that aligns, I’ll loop in our Solutions lead (Vivek) and CS (Monica) to prep the tech session.

Thanks — enjoyed the conversation.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: Quanta_MAPlike_Draft_20270305.pdf] [Attachment: redwood-dedicated-pricing-qs.xlsx]

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@quanta.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@quanta.ai
Date: 2027-03-02T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment modes & migration path (quick recap + next steps)

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side:

1) Traffic profile:
- Search/QA endpoint: steady 40 req/s daytime, spikes to ~120 req/s for short windows.
- Batch offline jobs: run nightly (2–3 hours) and need burstable GPU for embeddings generation.

2) Compliance:
- We need SOC2 + encryption-in-transit + KMS integration for key management. Private VPC would be ideal for regulated datasets, but we’d prefer to start on Dedicated if the SLA and network peering options are acceptable.

3) Migration:
- We want a plan that minimizes model output drift. Our research team keeps models tuned on the self-hosted cluster. Can Redwood support gradual traffic shifting and A/B comparison tooling?

4) Procurement asks:
- Ballpark monthly cost ranges for Dedicated with two reserved GPU nodes (NVIDIA A10G or equivalent) and for Private (VPC) baseline support.
- Typical lead time for Dedicated reservation and for setting up a Private VPC deployment.

Yes to a technical deep-dive. Who from Redwood should join? I’ll invite our infra lead (cc’d procurement if needed).

—
Daniel Park
Head of ML Infrastructure | Quanta Systems
daniel.park@quanta.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@quanta.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment modes & migration path (quick recap + next steps)

Appreciate the details, Daniel — that helps a lot. Quick answers inline and proposed next steps below.

Traffic & burst: Dedicated can handle steady 40 req/s with margin; for spikes to 120 req/s we recommend configuring burst capacity or autoscaling policies (we’ll size based on p99 latency targets). Nightly batch jobs are a common pattern — we can support burst via reserved+burst or spot-backed worker pools depending on cost profile.

Compliance & networking: We can provide SOC2 artefacts and support KMS integrations. For Private VPC, typical setup time is 6–8 weeks (depending on network reviews and provisioned on-prem options). Dedicated lead time is typically 2–4 weeks to provision reserved capacity in a region.

Migration & quality: Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts plus side-by-side variant routing; we also include evaluation hooks so you can compare outputs and trigger regressions alerts against your prompt sets. That’s standard in our Redwood Console.

Procurement asks: I’m attaching a draft MAP and a Dedicated pricing workbook with ballpark monthly ranges for 2 reserved GPU nodes, including an optional burst policy and Private VPC baseline estimate. See attachments.

Proposed next steps
- Schedule 60-min tech deep-dive: Vivek (solutions SE) + Monica (CS) will run network/SOC2 & migration plan. Please share 2 windows next week — we’ll block one.
- Procurement intro: loop in procurement@quanta.ai and we’ll follow with a formal SOW and pricing term sheet.

If that works I’ll finalize the MAP and send a calendar invite.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: Quanta_MAPlike_Draft_20270305.pdf] [Attachment: redwood-dedicated-pricing-qs.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-05T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Quanta Systems — prep for tech deep-dive (info + asks)

Vivek / Monica — prepping for the call with Quanta (Daniel Park). Summary and asks below.

Summary
- They want to migrate from mixed third-party LLM API + self-hosted clusters to Redwood. Short-term: evaluate Hosted/Dedicated. Mid-term: consider Private VPC for regulated data.
- Traffic: 40 req/s steady, spikes to 120 req/s; nightly batch embedding jobs (2–3 hrs).
- Compliance: SOC2 required + KMS integration; on-prem may be needed for certain datasets.

Asks / prep items
1) Vivek — please prepare:
   - Proposed Dedicated sizing for 2 reserved nodes (operators: A10G-equivalent), autoscale/burst policy recommendations, and expected p50/p95/p99 latencies for their traffic profile.
   - Short runbook for gradual migration (canary/A-B + KV cache handling).
   - Notes on KMS integration and networking (VPC peering options).

2) Monica — please prepare:
   - SOC2 artefacts checklist and typical timelines for a Private VPC onboarding.
   - CS playbook for POC (2–4 week milestones) and success metrics we’ll propose.

3) Pricing: I’ve attached the draft workbook; we should reconcile numbers before the call.

Call is tentatively scheduled for next week pending Daniel’s availability. I’ll circulate the calendar invite once they confirm.

Thanks — let me know if you need any additional context from the discovery notes.

—
Marissa
